# Commands

<!-- Generated by `tenon-cli commands --markdown --out docs/commands.md`; a test fails when it is out of date. -->

Everything Tenon does to a part is a command with JSON parameters: the ribbon, scripts (`tenon-cli run`, see [scripts.md](scripts.md)) and agents ([mcp.md](mcp.md)) all go through the same registry. Units are millimetres and radians. *Undoable* commands edit the part as one step that `edit.undo` reverts.

| Command | Name | Parameters | Undoable |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document.rename` | Rename Part | name: text | yes |
| `document.material` | Material | name: a material of the library (see document.materials), or null for none; density (g/cm^3) and color ("#rrggbb") to change them or to describe a material of one's own | yes |
| `document.appearance` | Appearance | color: "#rrggbb", the part's own colour in place of its material's; or null to go back to the material's | yes |
| `document.materials` | Materials | the material library (name, density in g/cm^3, colour) and the part's material, appearance, density and colour | no |
| `table.show` | Design Table | the part's design table: its parameters (columns), its rows and the active one; null without one | no |
| `table.create` | Create Design Table | columns: [parameter names] (plain values, not ones worked out by an equation); row: the name of the first row, which is the part as it stands (default "Size 1") | yes |
| `table.delete` | Delete Design Table | the part keeps the active row's values | yes |
| `table.add_row` | Add Row | name; values: {"parameter": number, ...} (the rest as the active row; lengths in mm, angles in degrees) | yes |
| `table.remove_row` | Remove Row | name (not the active row) | yes |
| `table.rename_row` | Rename Row | name, to | yes |
| `table.set` | Set Table Value | row, column (a parameter name), value; in the active row this changes the part | yes |
| `table.add_column` | Add Table Column | name: a parameter; every row gets its present value | yes |
| `table.remove_column` | Remove Table Column | name; the parameter keeps its value | yes |
| `table.activate` | Activate Row | row: the part takes that row's values | yes |
| `sketch.create` | New Sketch | plane: "xy" \| "yz" \| "xz" (default xy), or face: a face reference from model.face_ref; project_origin (default true: a fixed point at the part origin, returned as `origin`); project_edges (default false): on a face, the face's edges are shown in the sketch as reference geometry, as sketch.project does (or give `edges` and `geometry` as for sketch.project). Returns the feature, and the entities `projected` | yes |
| `sketch.point` | Point | sketch, x, y | yes |
| `sketch.line` | Line | sketch; start (point id) or x1, y1; end (point id) or x2, y2 | yes |
| `sketch.circle` | Circle | sketch; center (point id) or cx, cy; r. Returns the circle and its centre point (`center`) | yes |
| `sketch.arc` | Arc | sketch; center or cx, cy; start or x1, y1; end or x2, y2 (counter-clockwise). Returns the arc and its points (`center`, `start`, `end`) | yes |
| `sketch.arc3` | Three-Point Arc | sketch, x1, y1, x2, y2 (a point on the arc), x3, y3 | yes |
| `sketch.rectangle` | Rectangle | sketch, x1, y1, x2, y2 (opposite corners); returns lines and corners (the first at x1, y1) | yes |
| `sketch.polygon` | Polygon | sketch, cx, cy, x, y (a corner), sides | yes |
| `sketch.spline` | Spline | sketch, points: [[x, y], ...] (control points), degree (default 3) | yes |
| `sketch.constrain` | Constrain | sketch, constraint: {"type": "horizontal", "line": 3} etc. (see docs/commands.md); equation: drives a new dimension (e.g. "width / 2"); at_x, at_y: where a dimension's value is shown (default: beside its geometry); driven: true for a dimension that follows the sketch instead of setting it (shown in parentheses), or "auto" to make it driven only when a driving one would be one too many | yes |
| `sketch.place_dimension` | Move Dimension | sketch, constraint (a dimension's id), x, y: where its value is shown; its dimension line runs through there | yes |
| `sketch.set_dimension` | Edit Dimension | sketch, constraint (id); value (mm or rad), or equation (e.g. "d0 / 2", lengths in mm, angles in degrees) | yes |
| `sketch.set_driven` | Driven Dimension | sketch, constraint (id), driven: true (the dimension follows the sketch from now on) or false (it holds the sketch at the value it shows; refused when the sketch is held without it) | yes |
| `sketch.remove_constraint` | Delete Constraint | sketch, constraint (id) | yes |
| `sketch.drag` | Drag Point | sketch, point (id), x, y | yes |
| `sketch.delete` | Delete | sketch, entities: [ids] | yes |
| `sketch.construction` | Construction | sketch, entity (id), on (default true) | yes |
| `sketch.centerline` | Centerline | sketch, entity (a line's id), on (default true). A centre line is the axis a revolution turns about unless told otherwise, and a dimension to it is a diameter; it still bounds profiles | yes |
| `sketch.project` | Project Geometry | sketch; edge or edges: edge references (model.edge_ref), or face: a face reference whose edges are all projected. The edges are shown in the sketch as reference geometry: it follows the part, other geometry is constrained and dimensioned to it, and it bounds profiles. Only edges made before the sketch; straight and circular ones. flat: true (Project Flat Pattern, in a sketch on a side of a sheet metal part) shows each edge where it lies with the sheet laid flat from the sketch's face, so the faces beyond a bend can be drawn on for a cut across it. geometry: what each of `edges` is on the sketch plane (for callers without a kernel). Returns the entities, and why any edge of a face was left out | yes |
| `sketch.break_link` | Break Link | sketch, entities: [ids of projected curves or points]. They stay where they are, become the sketch's own geometry and no longer follow the part | yes |
| `sketch.fillet` | Sketch Fillet | sketch, point (corner id), radius | yes |
| `sketch.trim` | Trim | sketch, curve (id), x, y (the piece to remove) | yes |
| `sketch.offset` | Offset | sketch, curves: [ids], distance (positive: outward / left) | yes |
| `sketch.mirror` | Mirror | sketch, entities: [ids], axis (line id) | yes |
| `sketch.move` | Move | sketch, entities: [ids], dx, dy; copy (default false: with it the geometry stays and a copy is made). What is joined or constrained to the geometry follows; what holds it where it is refuses the move. Returns the entities moved, or the copies | yes |
| `sketch.rotate` | Rotate | sketch, entities: [ids], cx, cy (the point to turn about), angle (rad, counter-clockwise); copy. Level and upright constraints within what turns are dropped (swapped by quarter turns) | yes |
| `sketch.scale` | Scale | sketch, entities: [ids], cx, cy (the point that stays), factor; copy. Dimensions within what is scaled are scaled with it | yes |
| `sketch.extend` | Extend | sketch, curve (a line or an arc), x, y (near the end to extend). The end goes on along the curve to the nearest curve in its way and is held on it | yes |
| `sketch.split` | Split | sketch, curve (a line, an arc or a circle), x, y (near the crossing to split at). The curve becomes two that share a point held on the curve crossing there; returns the new one | yes |
| `sketch.pattern.rect` | Rectangular Sketch Pattern | sketch, entities: [ids]; along (a line's id) or dx, dy: the direction; count (the original counted), spacing; and for a second direction count2, spacing2 and along2 or dx2, dy2 (default: square to the first). Returns the copies, which are geometry of their own (they do not follow the original afterwards) | yes |
| `sketch.pattern.circular` | Circular Sketch Pattern | sketch, entities: [ids]; center (a point's id) or cx, cy; count (the original counted); angle (rad, default a whole turn, divided evenly; less reaches from the first to the last). Returns the copies | yes |
| `sketch.slot` | Slot | sketch, x1, y1, x2, y2, width; by: centers (default: the two points are the centres of the round ends) \| overall (they are the ends of the slot) \| center (the middle of the slot and one centre). Returns its lines, arcs and the centre points of its ends | yes |
| `sketch.rectangle_center` | Rectangle from Centre | sketch, cx, cy (its centre), x, y (a corner); returns its lines and the centre point, which stays its centre | yes |
| `sketch.rectangle3` | Three-Point Rectangle | sketch, x1, y1, x2, y2 (one side), x3, y3 (a point on the opposite side): a rectangle at any angle | yes |
| `sketch.arc_tangent` | Tangent Arc | sketch, from (the free end point of a line or an arc), x, y (where the arc ends): an arc that carries on from the curve, tangent to it | yes |
| `sketch.info` | Sketch Info | sketch | no |
| `model.extrude` | Extrude | sketch; distance (plus backward: a second distance the other way), or symmetric: total, or through_all: true; reverse; operation: join \| cut \| new_body \| intersect; regions: the closed regions to use (default: every outer one), each as sketch.info lists it under `select`: [curve ids] for what those curves enclose, or {left: [ids], right: [ids], nth} for one region of a divided sketch; taper (radians the sides lean in as they leave the sketch, negative to lean out; one distance or through_all only) | yes |
| `model.revolve` | Revolve | sketch; axis: line id or "x" \| "y" \| "z" (default: the sketch's centre line, when it has one); angle (rad, default full); symmetric; operation; regions | yes |
| `model.fillet` | Fillet | edges: [edge references from model.edge_ref], radius | yes |
| `model.chamfer` | Chamfer | edges: [edge references]; distance; and either distance2 or angle (rad) with reference: a face reference for the first distance | yes |
| `model.shell` | Shell | thickness; remove: [face references] (faces to open, default none); outside (default false: walls grow inwards) | yes |
| `model.hole` | Hole | sketch; points: [point ids] (default: the sketch's centre points, i.e. points on no curve); diameter; depth or through_all: true; type: simple \| counterbore (counterbore_diameter, counterbore_depth) \| countersink (countersink_diameter, countersink_angle: rad, default 90 deg); tip_angle (rad, default 118 deg) or flat_bottom: true; reverse (drill along the sketch normal) | yes |
| `model.rib` | Rib | sketch; lines: [line ids] (default: its open lines); thickness (half on each side of the sketch plane); distance (default: until it meets the part); flip | yes |
| `model.sweep` | Sweep | sketch (the profile); regions; path_sketch; path: [line and arc ids], joined end to end (default: every line and arc of path_sketch that is not construction); the sweep starts at the end nearer the profile; fixed (keep the profile's orientation; default: turn it with the path); operation | yes |
| `model.coil` | Coil | sketch (the profile, off the axis); regions; axis: x \| y \| z, a line id of the sketch, or {"work": id}; pitch (mm per turn); turns; left (left-handed); operation | yes |
| `model.loft` | Loft | sections: [sketch ids], two or more in order, each with one closed profile; ruled (flat sides between sections); operation | yes |
| `model.draft` | Draft | faces: [face references] (the faces to tilt, on one body); the neutral plane, where the faces stay put: plane ("xy" \| "yz" \| "xz"), face (a planar face reference) or work_plane (id); angle (radians from the plane's normal, the pull direction); reverse (tilt the other way) | yes |
| `model.split` | Split | the cutting plane: plane ("xy" \| "yz" \| "xz"), face (a planar face reference) or work_plane (id); keep: "both" (two bodies, default) \| "front" (the side the plane's normal points to) \| "back"; body: a face reference on the one body to split (default: every body the plane passes through) | yes |
| `model.combine` | Combine | base: a face reference on the body that stays; tools: [face references], one on each other body; operation: "join" (default) \| "cut" \| "intersect"; keep_tools (default false: the other bodies are used up) | yes |
| `model.thread` | Thread | face: a face reference on a round shaft or hole; pitch (mm; default: the ISO coarse pitch for the face's diameter, following it); designation (text for drawings; default "M<diameter>x<pitch>"); length (mm from the start end; default the whole face); reverse (start from the other end); left (left-handed); modelled (cut the groove into the part; default false: cosmetic) | yes |
| `model.pattern.rect` | Rectangular Pattern | features: [feature ids]; direction: "x" \| "y" \| "z" or an edge reference (straight edge); count; spacing; reverse; optional direction2, count2, spacing2, reverse2 | yes |
| `model.pattern.circular` | Circular Pattern | features: [feature ids]; axis: "x" \| "y" \| "z", an edge reference (straight or circular edge) or a face reference (cylinder or cone); count; angle (rad, default a full turn: copies spread evenly); reverse | yes |
| `model.mirror` | Mirror | features: [feature ids]; plane: "xy" \| "yz" \| "xz", or face: a planar face reference | yes |
| `work.plane` | Work Plane | by: offset (base: plane, distance) \| angle (base: plane, axis: in the base plane, angle: rad) \| midplane (a, b: parallel planes); a plane is "xy" \| "yz" \| "xz", a face reference or {"work": plane id} | yes |
| `work.axis` | Work Axis | axis: "x" \| "y" \| "z", an edge reference, a cylindrical face reference or {"work": id}; or a, b: two planes it lies on | yes |
| `work.point` | Work Point | edge: a circular edge reference (its centre); or axis and plane (where they meet) | yes |
| `feature.add` | Add Feature | kind: a feature definition as in model.tree / the file format; equations: {value field: equation} | yes |
| `param.list` | Parameters | every model parameter (named dimensions and feature values) and user parameter | no |
| `param.add` | Add Parameter | name; equation (e.g. "40 mm", "width / 2"); unit: mm \| deg \| ul (default mm); comment | yes |
| `param.set` | Set Parameter | name; equation: text, or a number (for a model parameter: its plain value, no equation), or null to drop a model parameter's equation; comment | yes |
| `param.rename` | Rename Parameter | name, to: the new name (every equation using it follows) | yes |
| `param.delete` | Delete Parameter | name: a user parameter no equation uses | yes |
| `feature.update` | Edit Feature | feature (id), kind: the feature definition as in model.tree / the file format; equations: {value field: equation} (e.g. {"/extent/distance": "d0 * 2"}) | yes |
| `feature.rename` | Rename Feature | feature, name | yes |
| `feature.suppress` | Suppress | feature, suppressed (default true) | yes |
| `feature.delete` | Delete Feature | feature | yes |
| `feature.end_of_part` | Move End of Part | before: the feature the marker goes just above (it and later ones are rolled back); omit or null for the end | yes |
| `feature.move` | Reorder Feature | feature; before: the feature it goes just above (omit or null: last, above the End of Part); sketches only it uses go along | yes |
| `edit.undo` | Undo | none | no |
| `edit.redo` | Redo | none | no |
| `model.tree` | Model Tree | none | no |
| `model.regenerate` | Regenerate | none | no |
| `model.mass` | Mass Properties | density (g/cm^3; default: the part's material's, or 1 without one). Per body: volume (mm^3), area (mm^2), mass (g), centre of mass (mm), inertia about it (g mm^2); and the total mass, the density used and the material | no |
| `model.threads` | Threads | every thread on the part: its feature, designation, pitch, major diameter, internal (in a hole), length, left, modelled, and where on its axis it starts and which way it runs | no |
| `model.topology` | Topology | none | no |
| `model.faces` | Faces | body (default 0) | no |
| `model.edges` | Edges | body (default 0): every edge with the names of its two faces | no |
| `model.work` | Work Features | where every work plane, axis and point is | no |
| `model.measure` | Measure | a, and optionally b: {"face": face reference} \| {"edge": edge reference} \| {"body": n, "face" or "edge": index}; one gives its area, length or diameter, two give the distance (with the nearest points) and the angle | no |
| `model.broken` | Broken References | the failing feature, its message, and each of its references that no longer finds its face or edge: path (in the feature definition), kind (edge or face) and up to three candidates (reference, distance in mm), nearest first | no |
| `model.repair` | Repair Reference | feature; path (from model.broken); with: the edge or face reference to use instead (from model.broken, model.edge_ref or model.face_ref) | yes |
| `sheet.defaults` | Sheet Metal Defaults | Makes the part a sheet metal part and sets its rule. Sizes, each a number (mm) or an equation: thickness, bend_radius, relief_width, relief_depth, min_remnant, corner_size, gap, and k_factor (0 to 1); they are the parameters Thickness, BendRadius, BendReliefWidth, BendReliefDepth, MinimumRemnant, CornerReliefSize, GapSize and KFactor. relief: "straight" \| "round" (the cut beside a bend narrower than its edge); corner: "round" \| "square" \| "trim" (the relief where two bends meet at a corner, centred where their centre lines cross). Returns the rule as it now is | yes |
| `sheet.info` | Sheet Metal Rule | the part's sheet metal rule and sizes, or sheet_metal: false | no |
| `sheet.face` | Face | sketch; regions; flip (the thickness goes behind the sketch plane); operation: "join" (default) \| "new_body". A closed profile made one Thickness thick | yes |
| `sheet.flange` | Flange | edges: [edge references] (straight edges of the sheet's rim; the flange bends towards the side each is on); height; angle (rad, default a quarter turn); datum: "outer" (default: the height is overall) \| "inner" \| "tangent"; position: "inside" (default: the flange's outer face goes through the edge) \| "adjacent" (the bend starts at the edge) \| "outside" \| "tangent"; flip (bend to the other side); radius (default BendRadius); width (in the middle of the edge) or offsets: [from the start, from the end] (default: the whole edge). Edges that meet at a corner get the rule's corner relief, and their walls are brought together to leave the rule's gap (miter: false leaves each wall ending where its bend does). Edges on the tops of two walls either side of a corner are mitred the same way: lips turned in over a tray do not share its corners | yes |
| `sheet.hem` | Hem | edges: [edge references] (straight edges of the sheet's rim; the hem folds towards the side each is on); type: "single" (default: folded flat back over the sheet) \| "double" (folded over twice) \| "rolled" (a bend and nothing after it) \| "teardrop" (rolled past half a turn, then straight back down to the sheet); gap (single, double: between the layers; default half a Thickness) and length (overall, from the outside of the fold; default four Thicknesses); radius (rolled, teardrop: inside; default BendRadius) and angle (rad; default 270 degrees rolled, 190 teardrop); flip (fold to the other side); width or offsets: [from the start, from the end] as for sheet.flange | yes |
| `sheet.contour_flange` | Contour Flange | sketch (an open profile: lines and arcs end to end; corners between lines become bends, an arc is a bend as drawn); distance (how far the profile is pushed out of its plane); direction: "default" \| "flipped" \| "symmetric"; position: "default" (the sheet goes on the inside of the profile's first corner) \| "flipped" \| "symmetric"; radius (inside, of the bends made at corners; default BendRadius); operation: "join" (default) \| "new_body". Or along edges of the sheet: edges: [edge references] (straight edges of its rim; the sketch is square to the first and the profile starts at that edge, the side of the sheet the edge is on running on into it, with a bend where it leaves at an angle, for which the sheet is cut back) with width or offsets as for sheet.flange; distance, direction and position then say nothing | yes |
| `sheet.corner_seam` | Corner Seam | edges: [two edge references]: the edge at the end of each of two faces that are bent up from one sheet and come together at a square corner (flanges made apart: edges of one flange close their own corners); the first face's, then the second's. Their bends are ended where the two bend lines cross, the faces brought together, and the corner relieved. seam: "symmetric" (default: both stop the gap apart) \| "overlap" (the first runs across the end of the second) \| "reverse_overlap"; overlap (how much of the other's thickness is covered, 0 to 1; default 1); gap (default GapSize); relief: "round" \| "square" \| "trim" and relief_size (default: the rule's) | yes |
| `sheet.corner_rip` | Corner Rip | edges: [edge references]: each the edge of a square corner where two walls of the sheet meet with no seam between them (the corner of a shelled box, say), its outside edge or its inside one. The corner is opened along the edge, as far as the edge goes: seam: "symmetric" (default: both walls stop where their inner faces are the gap apart, and the corner between them goes) \| "overlap" (the first wall keeps the corner and the second stops the gap short of it; the first is the wall whose face the edge reference names first) \| "reverse_overlap"; overlap (how much of the other wall's thickness the wall that keeps the corner covers, 0 to 1; default 1); gap (default GapSize). Bends are not made of the sharp edges that are left | yes |
| `sheet.cut_across_bend` | Cut Across Bend | sketch (on a flat face of the sheet, its profile of lines, arcs and circles drawn as on the flat pattern: past an edge of the face that is a bend line it lies on the bend, then on the face beyond); regions; distance (how deep from the side the sketch is on; default and at most Thickness: through). The profile is cut out of every face and bend it lies on with the sheet laid flat from the sketch's face, so the cut goes round the bends and is the profile in the flat pattern | yes |
| `sheet.cut_normal` | Cut Normal | sketch (on any plane that looks at the sheet: a face of it, or a work plane over it at any angle; its profile of lines, arcs and circles); regions; distance (how deep from the side of the sheet that looks at the sketch; default and at most Thickness: through). The profile is cut out of every flat face and bend of that side it is seen on, looking along the sketch's normal, and each is cut square to itself: a cut whose walls are square to the sheet whatever the angle of the sketch, so the flat pattern has one clean outline. (On a face parallel to the sketch it is the profile; at an angle, or on a bend, the profile as it is seen there.) | yes |
| `sheet.bend` | Bend | edges: [two edge references]: a straight edge of the rim of each of two faces of the sheet that do not touch (a face made apart from the rest is one), running alongside one another (for a sharp edge where two faces touch, see sheet.sharp_bend). The faces are joined by a bend along as much of the edges as lie side by side, each face trimmed or extended to where the bend begins. radius (inside; default BendRadius). Faces in planes that cross take one bend, tangent to both. Faces in parallel planes take two, as double says: "fix_edges" (default: two equal bends between the edges as they are), "45_degree" or "90_degree" (two bends of that angle and a face between them: side by side an S, one over the other a U at 90), "full_radius" (one over the other: half a circle, as wide inside as the faces are apart); flip_fixed (the second edge stays where it is and the first face is trimmed or extended, not the other way round) | yes |
| `sheet.sharp_bend` | Bend on Sharp Edges | edges: [edge references]: each the edge of a sharp corner where two faces of the sheet meet with no bend between them (the edges of a shelled box, say), its outside edge or its inside one. Every corner is cleared back to where a bend begins on either face, for the length of its edge, and the bend is put in, tangent to both faces, as far along the edge as both faces still reach it: the outer faces stay where they are. radius (inside; default BendRadius). Edges that meet at a corner of the sheet are given together: their bends then end where their bend lines cross. A bend whose end would lie against sheet that runs on beside it is refused: open that corner first (sheet.corner_rip) | yes |
| `sheet.fold` | Fold | sketch (on a side of the sheet: a face of it, or a plane that lies on one) with a straight line across the face, from edge to edge; line: its id (default: the sketch's one line). The sheet on one side of the line stays, the bend takes its allowance of sheet at the line, and the rest turns with it: nothing is added. angle (rad, default a quarter turn); radius (inside; default BendRadius); location: "centerline" (default: the line is the middle of the bend) \| "start" (the bend starts at the line) \| "end"; flip_side (the other side of the line folds: as drawn, the side to its left seen from the sketch's side of the sheet); flip_direction (down, away from the sketch's side, not up towards it) | yes |
| `sheet.a_side` | Define A-Side | face: a flat face reference, the side that is up when the flat pattern lies on the table; without it, the largest flat face | yes |
| `sheet.flat_pattern` | Create Flat Pattern | on (default true): the part has a flat pattern, shown in the browser; false deletes it. (sheet.flat works it out either way.) | yes |
| `sheet.flat` | Flat Pattern | The part laid flat: length and width (the sheet it is cut from), area, cut_length (round the outline and every hole), holes, and each bend's angle (rad), inside radius, allowance (its width in the flat), up (bent towards the A side) and centre lines. face: the A side (default: the part's, else the largest flat face); body (default: the only one); curves: true adds the outlines (outer, inner) as lines, arcs, circles and polylines | no |
| `model.edge_ref` | Edge Reference | faces: [face origin, face origin] (the two faces the edge joins); or at: [x, y, z], a point on the edge away from its ends; or body (default 0) and edge (index from model.edges) | no |
| `model.face_ref` | Face Reference | origin: {"type": "cap", "feature": id, "end": "start" \| "end"} or {"type": "side", "feature": id, "curve": id}; or at: [x, y, z], a point inside the face; or body (default 0) and face (index from model.faces) | no |
| `model.find` | Find Geometry | Faces or edges of the part by what they are and where, each with a reference to it. what: faces \| edges; body (default: every body); kind: plane \| cylinder \| cone \| sphere \| torus \| other (faces), line \| circle \| arc \| other (edges); facing: the way a flat face looks, as +x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z, top, bottom, left, right, front, back or [x, y, z]; along: the direction of a straight edge, or of the axis of a round face or edge; feature: made by that feature; hole: true for the walls of holes, false for shafts; radius; most: of what is found, only the furthest that way (top, -x, ...), or the largest or smallest. Returns count and found: each with body, its number (face or edge), name, reference (null when it cannot be referred to yet), kind and its measures; and, when a feature fails, error (feature, message): what is found is then of the part as far as it rebuilt | no |
| `study.new` | New Study | A stress study of the part: where it is held and what pushes on it. name (default Study1, Study2...). Returns the study as study.list gives it | yes |
| `study.rename` | Rename Study | study (default: the part's only one); name | yes |
| `study.delete` | Delete Study | study (default: the part's only one) | yes |
| `study.fix` | Fixed Support | Holds faces still. study (default: the part's only one); faces: [face references]; name. Returns the study, and support: the new support's id | yes |
| `study.force` | Force | A force spread over faces. study; faces: [face references]; newtons: the whole force; direction: the way it pushes, as +x, -z, top, bottom ... or [x, y, z] (default, or normal: square to each face, into it; negative newtons pull); name. Returns the study, and load: the new load's id | yes |
| `study.pressure` | Pressure | A pressure on faces, square to them and into them. study; faces: [face references]; megapascals (N/mm^2; negative pulls); name. Returns the study, and load: the new load's id | yes |
| `study.set` | Change Support or Load | Changes a support or a load of a study: what is given takes the place of what it had. study; item: its id; faces: [face references]; name; of a force: newtons, direction (as for study.force, or normal: square to its faces); of a pressure: megapascals | yes |
| `study.remove` | Remove Support or Load | study; item: the id of a support or a load of it | yes |
| `study.mesh_size` | Element Size | How large the elements are that the part is divided into to work the study out. study; size (mm; null: chosen from the part's size) | yes |

With as_one false the steps before a failure stand. Returns each step's result | no |

## Constraints

`sketch.constrain` takes one of these as `constraint` (the numbers are entity ids from the sketch commands). Dimensions (`distance` to `diameter`) drive the geometry; change them with `sketch.set_dimension`.

- `{"type":"coincident","a":1,"b":2}`
- `{"type":"point_on_curve","point":1,"curve":2}`
- `{"type":"horizontal","line":1}`
- `{"type":"vertical","line":1}`
- `{"type":"parallel","a":1,"b":2}`
- `{"type":"perpendicular","a":1,"b":2}`
- `{"type":"collinear","a":1,"b":2}`
- `{"type":"tangent","a":1,"b":2}`
- `{"type":"concentric","a":1,"b":2}`
- `{"type":"equal","a":1,"b":2}`
- `{"type":"symmetric","a":1,"b":2,"axis":3}`
- `{"type":"midpoint","point":1,"line":2}`
- `{"type":"fix","point":1}`
- `{"type":"distance","a":1,"b":2,"value":10.0}`
- `{"type":"horizontal_distance","a":1,"b":2,"value":10.0}`
- `{"type":"vertical_distance","a":1,"b":2,"value":10.0}`
- `{"type":"length","line":1,"value":10.0}`
- `{"type":"angle","a":1,"b":2,"value":0.5}`
- `{"type":"radius","curve":1,"value":5.0}`
- `{"type":"diameter","curve":1,"value":10.0}`
- `{"type":"linear_diameter","point":1,"axis":2,"value":10.0}`
